record_type_quote: Two different labs collaborated over the attempt to replicate both conceptually and directly the findings reported by Cannon and Woodward (2012).

targets.title: Infants generate goal-based action predictions.
targets.evidence_quote: Thus, one central point of this endeavor was to examine whether or not we could (conceptually or directly) replicate Cannon and Woodward (2012) and contribute thus to the theoretical debate by examining the robustness of a key finding.
targets.outcome_quote: However, despite our systematic variation of any other factors that could have had an influence on infants’ action perception (such as type of agent, presence of an occluder or number of learning- and test trials), we failed to replicate the findings of Cannon and Woodward (2012) across all our experiments and labs.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall failure verdict covers both labs and all conceptual and direct replications.

targets.authors: Daum, M. M., Attig, M., Gunawan, R., Prinz, W., & Gredebäck, G.
targets.title: Actions seen through babies’ eyes: A dissociation between looking time and predictive gaze.
targets.evidence_quote: In the path-paradigm, we expected 11-month-olds and 32-month-olds to anticipate the old path, thus the novel goal, as the action is performed by a non-human agent (Daum et al., 2012).
targets.outcome_quote: Considering the path-paradigm with the animated agent, 11-month-olds looked longer towards the familiarized path leading to the novel goal. Hence results are similar to Study 1 and Daum et al. (2012).
targets.outcome_reasoning: New samples re-test the path-versus-goal result in animated-agent tasks. The paper explicitly describes agreement with Daum for infant and toddler path anticipations; adults also anticipate the goal in the animated path paradigm.

targets.authors: Pfundmair, M., Zwarg, C., Paulus, M., & Rimpel, A.
targets.title: Oxytocin promotes attention to social cues regardless of group membership.
targets.evidence_quote: We hypothesized to find anticipations towards the familiarized goal within the adult sample in both paradigms (Daum et al., 2012; Pfundmair et al., 2017).
targets.outcome_quote: Pfundmair et al. (2017) found that adults anticipated the goal of a grasping hand as well as of a grasping claw, which is in contrast to our findings.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Study 2 explicitly predicts adult goal anticipations from this prior finding and contrasts its observed adult hand-path anticipation with that result. The original oxytocin effect itself is not re-tested; target is the adult action-goal anticipation finding.

reasoning: Full-text title and all four authors match. New participants in two labs re-test goal-versus-path anticipation findings. Cannon and Woodward is the central replication target. Daum and Pfundmair are included because Study 2 explicitly predicts their previously reported age/agent findings and compares corresponding new-sample results; other method sources and general theoretical citations are excluded. Original study numbers are not specified. All verdicts concern the particular findings tested rather than every claim in the original papers.
